body.heading: Where in the world is Finland?
paragraphs: Finland is a country in Northern Europe, which is part of Europe.

body.heading: The capital city
paragraphs: The capital of Finland is Helsinki.

body.heading: Words you might hear
paragraphs: People in Finland speak Finnish and Swedish.

body.heading: Money in your pocket
paragraphs: The money of Finland is the euro. The euro is shared by many countries in Europe, so the same coins and notes work across borders.

body.heading: How big is Finland?
paragraphs: Finland covers about 338,000 square kilometres of land and inland water. That makes it about half the size of France.

body.heading: Two places we'd love to visit
paragraphs: Rovaniemi sits on the Arctic Circle, where families meet Santa in his village office all year, visit huskies and reindeer, and hunt the northern lights in winter.
Helsinki's harbour leads to Suomenlinna, a giant sea fortress spread over islands — ferries, tunnels, cannons and picnic lawns, all a short boat ride away.

body.heading: Think and talk
paragraphs: 1. Find Finland on a map or globe. Which continent is it on — and can you name a country that sits next to it?
2. Spark and Mango can visit only ONE of the two places in this article. Which should they choose — and what would you pack for the trip?
